**Kampong Bokok** (Malay: _Kampung Bokok_) or simply **Bokok**, is a village in Temburong District, Brunei, about 10 kilometres (6.2 mi) from the district town Bangar. The population was 160 in 2021.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampong_Bokok#cite_note-2) It is one of the villages within Mukim Bokok. The postcode is PE1951.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampong_Bokok#cite_note-postcode-3)

Kampong Bokok's historical name is the reason it is known as "Bokok." There are two tales concerning how the name "Bokok" came to be, according to the village elders. The first comes from _Sungai Bokok_ (Bokok River), a little river that empties into the Rataie River. Second, it originates from _takuyung_ (Potamides cerithium) known as _takuyung bakak_ in Murut. Due to its form, which resembles a human bending over, Malaysians commonly refer to it as Bokok.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampong_Bokok#cite_note-:02-4)
Kampong Bokok has a community of 464 people who live within its 63 hectares, 226 men and 238 women, in 2018. There are 395 Malays, 45 Ibans, and 24 other races among those. There are 419 Muslims overall, with the remaining members of various other faiths.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampong_Bokok#cite_note-:02-4)
Kampong Bokok produces a variety of sweets, including _wajid java_ and _wajid_ rice, for its own subsistence and not specifically to be turned into a product under _Majlis Perundingan Kampung_ (MPK) Bokok's _1 Kampung 1 Produk_ (1K1P) branding, just like other villages in Temburong District that each have different productions and products as an activity in the economic sector. According to its ketua kampung, these people are often invited by certain parties such as participating in Bandarku Ceria in Bandar Seri Begawan, hotels and so on to display and sell the results of their efforts there. Also on display to customers is _wajid_ which is an attraction of Temburong District in addition to Temburong Cendol and lobster.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampong_Bokok#cite_note-:02-4)

Kampung Bokok shares all the amenities the Government of Brunei provides for the convenience of the populace and inhabitants, including roads, a clean water supply, power, telephone lines, religious schools, mosques, and gathering places, much like other villages in the Temburong District. The villages also got financial aid in the form of old age pensions for 57 individuals, Community Development Department Assistance (JAPEM) for eight people, poor aid for seven, orphan aid for six, conversion aid for 21 persons, and OKU aid for one for disabled people.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampong_Bokok#cite_note-:02-4)
Bokok Religious School is the village's government school for the country's Islamic religious primary education.
The village mosque is Pengiran Haji Abu Bakar Mosque. It was inaugurated on 26 February 1988 and can accommodate 200 worshippers.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampong_Bokok#cite_note-mosque-5)

**Mukim Bokok** is a mukim in Temburong District, Brunei. It has an area of 136 square kilometres (53 sq mi);[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukim_Bokok#cite_note-:0-2) as of 2021, the population was 3,812.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukim_Bokok#cite_note-:3-4)

The mukim could be named after a village it encompasses, Kampong Bokok. Mukim Bokok's historical name is the reason it is known as "Bokok." There are two tales concerning how the name "Bokok" came to be, according to the village elders. The first comes from _Sungai Bokok_ (Bokok River), a little river that empties into the Rataie River. Second, it originates from _takuyung_ (Potamides cerithium) known as _takuyung bakak_ in Murut. Due to its form, which resembles a human bending over, Malaysians commonly refer to it as Bokok.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukim_Bokok#cite_note-:02-5)
The mukim is located in the west of the Temburong District to the south, bordering Mukim Bangar to the north-east, Mukim Amo to the east, and the Malaysian state of Sarawak to the south and west.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukim_Bokok#cite_note-:02-5)
As of 2021 census,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukim_Bokok#cite_note-:3-4) the population was 3,812 with 51.5% males and 48.5% females. The mukim had 797 households occupying 767 dwellings. The entire population lived in rural areas. According to statistical statistics provided by the penghulu in 2018, the total population by race as a whole consists of the Malay race totaling 2,746 people, the Murut tribe 55 people, the Iban tribe 688 people, the Chinese race 20 people and followed by other races/tribes which are 68 people.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukim_Bokok#cite_note-:02-5)

The late Pengiran Bendahara Pengiran Muda Haji Hashim gave the first Kampong Bokok mosque its formal opening on 21 June 1957. The land for this mosque was given to the Kampong Bokok locals by Awang Aji bin Dollah and Awang Ahmad bin Haji Malik.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukim_Bokok#cite_note-12) Additionally, the village has a primary school named Bokok Primary School. In 2008, the village was one of the most affected settlements by the sudden flood, with 55 homes ruined.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukim_Bokok#cite_note-13) Kampong Bokok produces traditional food with various flavors such as _kuih bahulu_ and various types of _Sapit_. In addition, the residents of Kampong Bokok also have _Kemajuan Pertanian Luar Bandar_ (KPLB) by producing several types of local fruit trees.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukim_Bokok#cite_note-:02-5)

**Mukim Bokok** is a mukim in Temburong District, Brunei. It has an area of 136 square kilometres (53 sq mi);[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukim_Bokok#cite_note-:0-2) as of 2021, the population was 3,812.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukim_Bokok#cite_note-:3-4)
texts.1:
The mukim could be named after a village it encompasses, Kampong Bokok. Mukim Bokok's historical name is the reason it is known as "Bokok." There are two tales concerning how the name "Bokok" came to be, according to the village elders. The first comes from _Sungai Bokok_ (Bokok River), a little river that empties into the Rataie River. Second, it originates from _takuyung_ (Potamides cerithium) known as _takuyung bakak_ in Murut. Due to its form, which resembles a human bending over, Malaysians commonly refer to it as Bokok.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukim_Bokok#cite_note-:02-5)
The mukim is located in the west of the Temburong District to the south, bordering Mukim Bangar to the north-east, Mukim Amo to the east, and the Malaysian state of Sarawak to the south and west.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukim_Bokok#cite_note-:02-5)
As of 2021 census,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukim_Bokok#cite_note-:3-4) the population was 3,812 with 51.5% males and 48.5% females. The mukim had 797 households occupying 767 dwellings. The entire population lived in rural areas. According to statistical statistics provided by the penghulu in 2018, the total population by race as a whole consists of the Malay race totaling 2,746 people, the Murut tribe 55 people, the Iban tribe 688 people, the Chinese race 20 people and followed by other races/tribes which are 68 people.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukim_Bokok#cite_note-:02-5)

The land for this mosque was given to the Kampong Bokok locals by Awang Aji bin Dollah and Awang Ahmad bin Haji Malik.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukim_Bokok#cite_note-12) Additionally, the village has a primary school named Bokok Primary School. **Kampong Bokok** (Malay: _Kampung Bokok_) or simply **Bokok**, is a village in Temburong District, Brunei, about 10 kilometres (6.2 mi) from the district town Bangar. The population was 160 in 2021.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampong_Bokok#cite_note-2) It is one of the villages within Mukim Bokok. The postcode is PE1951.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampong_Bokok#cite_note-postcode-3)
texts.1:
Kampong Bokok's historical name is the reason it is known as "Bokok." There are two tales concerning how the name "Bokok" came to be, according to the village elders. The first comes from _Sungai Bokok_ (Bokok River), a little river that empties into the Rataie River. Second, it originates from _takuyung_ (Potamides cerithium) known as _takuyung bakak_ in Murut. Due to its form, which resembles a human bending over, Malaysians commonly refer to it as Bokok.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampong_Bokok#cite_note-:02-4)
Kampong Bokok has a community of 464 people who live within its 63 hectares, 226 men and 238 women, in 2018. There are 395 Malays, 45 Ibans, and 24 other races among those. There are 419 Muslims overall, with the remaining members of various other faiths.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampong_Bokok#cite_note-:02-4)
Kampong Bokok produces a variety of sweets, including _wajid java_ and _wajid_ rice, for its own subsistence and not specifically to be turned into a product under _Majlis Perundingan Kampung_ (MPK) Bokok's _1 Kampung 1 Produk_ (1K1P) branding, just like other villages in Temburong District that each have different productions and products as an activity in the economic sector. According to its ketua kampung, these people are often invited by certain parties such as participating in Bandarku Ceria in Bandar Seri Begawan, hotels and so on to display and sell the results of their efforts there. Also on display to customers is _wajid_ which is an attraction of Temburong District in addition to Temburong Cendol and lobster.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampong_Bokok#cite_note-:02-4)
texts.2:
Kampung Bokok shares all the amenities the Government of Brunei provides for the convenience of the populace and inhabitants, including roads, a clean water supply, power, telephone lines, religious schools, mosques, and gathering places, much like other villages in the Temburong District. The villages also got financial aid in the form of old age pensions for 57 individuals, Community Development Department Assistance (JAPEM) for eight people, poor aid for seven, orphan aid for six, conversion aid for 21 persons, and OKU aid for one for disabled people.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampong_Bokok#cite_note-:02-4)
Bokok Religious School is the village's government school for the country's Islamic religious primary education.
The village mosque is Pengiran Haji Abu Bakar Mosque. It was inaugurated on 26 February 1988 and can accommodate 200 worshippers.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampong_Bokok#cite_note-mosque-5)

**Mukim Bokok** is a mukim in Temburong District, Brunei. It has an area of 136 square kilometres (53 sq mi);[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukim_Bokok#cite_note-:0-2) as of 2021, the population was 3,812.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukim_Bokok#cite_note-:3-4)

The mukim could be named after a village it encompasses, Kampong Bokok. Mukim Bokok's historical name is the reason it is known as "Bokok." There are two tales concerning how the name "Bokok" came to be, according to the village elders. The first comes from _Sungai Bokok_ (Bokok River), a little river that empties into the Rataie River. Second, it originates from _takuyung_ (Potamides cerithium) known as _takuyung bakak_ in Murut. Due to its form, which resembles a human bending over, Malaysians commonly refer to it as Bokok.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukim_Bokok#cite_note-:02-5)
The mukim is located in the west of the Temburong District to the south, bordering Mukim Bangar to the north-east, Mukim Amo to the east, and the Malaysian state of Sarawak to the south and west.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukim_Bokok#cite_note-:02-5)
As of 2021 census,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukim_Bokok#cite_note-:3-4) the population was 3,812 with 51.5% males and 48.5% females. The mukim had 797 households occupying 767 dwellings. The entire population lived in rural areas. According to statistical statistics provided by the penghulu in 2018, the total population by race as a whole consists of the Malay race totaling 2,746 people, the Murut tribe 55 people, the Iban tribe 688 people, the Chinese race 20 people and followed by other races/tribes which are 68 people.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukim_Bokok#cite_note-:02-5)

The late Pengiran Bendahara Pengiran Muda Haji Hashim gave the first Kampong Bokok mosque its formal opening on 21 June 1957. The land for this mosque was given to the Kampong Bokok locals by Awang Aji bin Dollah and Awang Ahmad bin Haji Malik.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukim_Bokok#cite_note-12) Additionally, the village has a primary school named Bokok Primary School. In 2008, the village was one of the most affected settlements by the sudden flood, with 55 homes ruined.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukim_Bokok#cite_note-13) Kampong Bokok produces traditional food with various flavors such as _kuih bahulu_ and various types of _Sapit_. In addition, the residents of Kampong Bokok also have _Kemajuan Pertanian Luar Bandar_ (KPLB) by producing several types of local fruit trees.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukim_Bokok#cite_note-:02-5)

**Kampong Bokok** (Malay: _Kampung Bokok_) or simply **Bokok**, is a village in Temburong District, Brunei, about 10 kilometres (6.2 mi) from the district town Bangar. The population was 160 in 2021.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampong_Bokok#cite_note-2) It is one of the villages within Mukim Bokok. The postcode is PE1951.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampong_Bokok#cite_note-postcode-3)

Kampong Bokok's historical name is the reason it is known as "Bokok." There are two tales concerning how the name "Bokok" came to be, according to the village elders. The first comes from _Sungai Bokok_ (Bokok River), a little river that empties into the Rataie River. Second, it originates from _takuyung_ (Potamides cerithium) known as _takuyung bakak_ in Murut. Due to its form, which resembles a human bending over, Malaysians commonly refer to it as Bokok.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampong_Bokok#cite_note-:02-4)
Kampong Bokok has a community of 464 people who live within its 63 hectares, 226 men and 238 women, in 2018. There are 395 Malays, 45 Ibans, and 24 other races among those. There are 419 Muslims overall, with the remaining members of various other faiths.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampong_Bokok#cite_note-:02-4)
Kampong Bokok produces a variety of sweets, including _wajid java_ and _wajid_ rice, for its own subsistence and not specifically to be turned into a product under _Majlis Perundingan Kampung_ (MPK) Bokok's _1 Kampung 1 Produk_ (1K1P) branding, just like other villages in Temburong District that each have different productions and products as an activity in the economic sector. According to its ketua kampung, these people are often invited by certain parties such as participating in Bandarku Ceria in Bandar Seri Begawan, hotels and so on to display and sell the results of their efforts there. Also on display to customers is _wajid_ which is an attraction of Temburong District in addition to Temburong Cendol and lobster.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampong_Bokok#cite_note-:02-4)

Kampung Bokok shares all the amenities the Government of Brunei provides for the convenience of the populace and inhabitants, including roads, a clean water supply, power, telephone lines, religious schools, mosques, and gathering places, much like other villages in the Temburong District. The villages also got financial aid in the form of old age pensions for 57 individuals, Community Development Department Assistance (JAPEM) for eight people, poor aid for seven, orphan aid for six, conversion aid for 21 persons, and OKU aid for one for disabled people.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampong_Bokok#cite_note-:02-4)
Bokok Religious School is the village's government school for the country's Islamic religious primary education.
The village mosque is Pengiran Haji Abu Bakar Mosque. It was inaugurated on 26 February 1988 and can accommodate 200 worshippers.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampong_Bokok#cite_note-mosque-5)

**Biography:**
Che Puan Sarimah Ibrahim, 44, is the mother of Tunku Sofia Najihah and wife to YM Tunku Nadzimuddin Tunku Mudzaffar.
Che Puan Sarimah is TV Host, Actress, Professional Emcee, has been a morning show radio announcer and Recording Artist who is well known and loved by Malaysians for the past 25 years since her debut on TV in 1997 on NTV7 hosting the RIM Chart Show and Kids NTV7. Her iconic fun, informative style of hosting earned her the reputation of being a versatile host for any show Fluently in Bahasa Malaysia and English.
She has won notable awards in the Music industry such as a Malaysian Grammy (That is AIM), Anugerah Skrin TV3 as Best TV Presenter and also an ERA Music Award to name just a few awards.
Che Puan Sarimah has emceed more than 700 company events in Malaysia and Internationally in the last 2 decades including events for Corporate clients, members of Royalty, multiple events involving three of Malaysia’s previous Prime Ministers, Foreign delegates and much more. LIVE Entertainment events and Protocol are her specialties.
Best known as a TV Host on The Disney Channel In 1998 and with her Hit Single ‘Kini Kau Tiada’ , Che Puan Sarimah is also an avid fitness enthusiast with a black belt in Karate Kenpo Seibukan, a Pilates and gym enthusiast who also loves boxing and power Yoga.
She has also produced and recorded an English single called ‘You On My Mind” recorded in London and also BM single entitled “Destinasiku” produced by Damian Mikhail back in 2016.

Makeup by: Epie
Hair by: Cindy Hor
In 2021 She released a charity single called “Harapan” – a bilingual song about mental health and suicide awareness – written and produced by Damian Mikhail once again.
Che Puan Sarimah has starred in iconic Malay Films such as Gerak Khas 3, MX3, Janji Diana and has also hosted the Asian version of the global hit TV show aired on the Hallmark Channel -“ The Biggest Loser Asia” which aired regionally across Asia.

She hosted her own pioneering talk Show “The Sarimah Show “ on TV3 Primetime and She has graced the cover of magazines such as GLAM Malaysia, Eh!, HerWorld, Jelita and has graced the cover of renowned “ Readers Digest Asia” Magazine.
Che Puan Sarimah Ibrahim is of Irish Malay Chinese heritage and studied Psychology as her Major in college. Due to her lived experience with mental health issues and her educational background- she is a passionate Celebrity Mental Health Advocate.
Mainly Growing up in Kilkenny & Dublin, Ireland, then in KL and the UAE before moving back to Malaysia to study and work independently at 18, Che Puan Sarimah is also an entrepreneur and founded her own Cosmetic Company Thrill By Sarimah Ibrahim in 2018 however she is now focused on business investments related to mental health.
Outfit and Photography by: Rizman Ruzaini
Makeup by: Epie
Hair by: Cindy Hor
Che Puan Sarimah has been an active Speaker and moderator in discussions and forums both online and offline focusing especially on topics related to mental health, womens welfare with a focus on postnatal depression, cyber ethics, suicide prevention and anxiety.
She has been the ambassador for Womens Centre For Change in Penang, a Cervical Cancer Awareness ambassador with MAKNA and an active speaker with MIASA Malaysia and was the Patron of MIASA (Mental Illness Awareness and Support Association) Malaysia 2021. She is currently a qualified Transformational Coach awarded her cert from Coach Masters Australia 2022.
Che Puan Sarimah currently lives In KL with her husband YM Tunku Nadzimuddin Tunku Mudzaffar, their 2.5 yr old daughter Tunku Sofia.
She currently emcees events, hosts entertainment TV shows such as Vazz Vaganza on Astro RIA, she hosted the Prestigious Malaysian Film Festival 2022 LIVE on RTM2 and the first ever inaugural LIVE IKON Sports Awards Harian Metro for Mediaprima.
Her goal is to continue to spread awareness on all mental health causes particularly in Asia and help develop businesses associated to it.

**SI:** From a professional prospective, as an actress, since 1996 to date it will be hosting the AJL Awards (similar to the Grammy’s). I’ve co-hosted three times! Also acting. I start a new Astro TV series playing a Lawyer!

**SI:** Probably Oat… I feel it’s somewhere in the middle. Neutral. Can be a great addition to compliment other colours and is usually creamy and delicious in texture. LOL! Definitely not beige! Hehe.“

**SI:** As a youngster being on holiday with either grandparents and family in Ireland or Malaysia … I grew up learning the depths of both cultures and am very grateful for that.

**SI:**I told myself it will be over soon and it could be worse. I conducted over 200 zoom webinars where I was a speaker or moderator, or a host for mental health advocacy work. I also released a charity single called “Harapan” – a bilingual song about mental health and suicide awareness – written and produced by Damian Mikhail in collaboration with NGO AWAS.

**SI:** NOTE FROM ED: Sarimah read the question as BEST not LAST!

Che Puan Sarimah with her husband YM Tunku Nadzimuddin Tunku Mudzaffar and daughter Tunku Sofia.
**HOMME: Where did you go to school?**
**SI:** Kilkenny in Ireland. Subang Jaya and Shah Alam. All local schools which were tremendously good for my life and career. Dubai meant International schools. Wesley College Dublin and HELP University here in KL.
**HOMME: What inspires you?**
**SI:** People being really genuine and honest. That’s inspiring.
**HOMME: Tell us something we don’t know about you?**
**SI:** I’m a Black Belt in Karate. I love reading autobiographys. I’m secretly an introvert which surprises everyone!

**HOMME: What do you want to be remembered for?**
**SI:** By family … never giving up … and my constant pursuit of improving myself. That I didn’t simply settle. And as a genuine soul who craved for honesty.
**HOMME: What is your favourite activity in your freetime?**
**SI:** My only vices are coffee and working out. I really enjoy listening to debates with professional individuals. Listening to alternative opinions is educational for any ‘individual’s development.

**SI:** I did 301 scuba dives. On the last 301ist dive I ran out of air at 22 meters. I stopped diving! I ski-dived 7 times before I got married. I’m still here. Needless to say, I stopped diving after that… and after i got married… I never took that risk again… I do miss being deep underwater still though!

Outfit and Photography by: Rizman Ruzaini
Makeup by: Epie
Hair by: Cindy Hor
Empati Malaysia, a youth non-governmental organization (NGO) dedicated to fighting for youth’s mental health with empathy, is excited to announce the official launch of its organization and the appointment of Yang Mulia Che Puan Sarimah as its official spokesperson.
Founded by Syahida Zulkarnain, Empati Malaysia aims to promote mental health education, support, and resources to the community through collaborations with organizations such as Pusat Psikologi Jiwa Damai, Pusat Kecemerlangan Kesihatan Mental Kebangsaan, and Jabatan Kebajikan Masyarakat (JKM). The launch event, which will take place on March 25th, 2023, at Liberal Latte, Kuala Lumpur, will be graced by YB Adam Adli Abd Halim, Deputy Minister of Youth and Sports.
The launch event will be a momentous occasion for Empati Malaysia, as it aims to raise awareness and advocate for the mental health of young Malaysians. The organization believes empathy is a powerful tool in promoting mental health and is committed to providing mental health education, support, and resources to the community.
Empati Malaysia has been working tirelessly to promote mental health awareness and support among the youth in Malaysia. With the appointment of Che Puan Sarimah, a well-known personality in the country and an active mental health advocate, the organization hopes to reach a wider audience and make a bigger impact in the community.
Che Puan Sarimah’s passion and dedication to the cause of mental health aligns perfectly with the goals and objectives of Empati Malaysia. As a spokesperson, she will work closely with the organization to raise awareness about mental health issues among the youth and encourage them to seek help when needed.
Attendees can also expect an engaging and informative program during the launch ceremony, with speeches from Empati Malaysia’s founding members and special guests.
There will also be opportunities for attendees to learn more about Empati Malaysia’s programs and initiatives and to network with like-minded individuals.

**Biography:**
Che Puan Sarimah Ibrahim, 44, is the mother of Tunku Sofia Najihah and wife to YM Tunku Nadzimuddin Tunku Mudzaffar.
Che Puan Sarimah is TV Host, Actress, Professional Emcee, has been a morning show radio announcer and Recording Artist who is well known and loved by Malaysians for the past 25 years since her debut on TV in 1997 on NTV7 hosting the RIM Chart Show and Kids NTV7. Her iconic fun, informative style of hosting earned her the reputation of being a versatile host for any show Fluently in Bahasa Malaysia and English.
She has won notable awards in the Music industry such as a Malaysian Grammy (That is AIM), Anugerah Skrin TV3 as Best TV Presenter and also an ERA Music Award to name just a few awards.
Che Puan Sarimah has emceed more than 700 company events in Malaysia and Internationally in the last 2 decades including events for Corporate clients, members of Royalty, multiple events involving three of Malaysia’s previous Prime Ministers, Foreign delegates and much more. LIVE Entertainment events and Protocol are her specialties.
Best known as a TV Host on The Disney Channel In 1998 and with her Hit Single ‘Kini Kau Tiada’ , Che Puan Sarimah is also an avid fitness enthusiast with a black belt in Karate Kenpo Seibukan, a Pilates and gym enthusiast who also loves boxing and power Yoga.
She has also produced and recorded an English single called ‘You On My Mind” recorded in London and also BM single entitled “Destinasiku” produced by Damian Mikhail back in 2016.

Makeup by: Epie
Hair by: Cindy Hor
In 2021 She released a charity single called “Harapan” – a bilingual song about mental health and suicide awareness – written and produced by Damian Mikhail once again.
Che Puan Sarimah has starred in iconic Malay Films such as Gerak Khas 3, MX3, Janji Diana and has also hosted the Asian version of the global hit TV show aired on the Hallmark Channel -“ The Biggest Loser Asia” which aired regionally across Asia.

She hosted her own pioneering talk Show “The Sarimah Show “ on TV3 Primetime and She has graced the cover of magazines such as GLAM Malaysia, Eh!, HerWorld, Jelita and has graced the cover of renowned “ Readers Digest Asia” Magazine.
Che Puan Sarimah Ibrahim is of Irish Malay Chinese heritage and studied Psychology as her Major in college. Due to her lived experience with mental health issues and her educational background- she is a passionate Celebrity Mental Health Advocate.
Mainly Growing up in Kilkenny & Dublin, Ireland, then in KL and the UAE before moving back to Malaysia to study and work independently at 18, Che Puan Sarimah is also an entrepreneur and founded her own Cosmetic Company Thrill By Sarimah Ibrahim in 2018 however she is now focused on business investments related to mental health.

Che Puan Sarimah has been an active Speaker and moderator in discussions and forums both online and offline focusing especially on topics related to mental health, womens welfare with a focus on postnatal depression, cyber ethics, suicide prevention and anxiety.
She has been the ambassador for Womens Centre For Change in Penang, a Cervical Cancer Awareness ambassador with MAKNA and an active speaker with MIASA Malaysia and was the Patron of MIASA (Mental Illness Awareness and Support Association) Malaysia 2021. She is currently a qualified Transformational Coach awarded her cert from Coach Masters Australia 2022.
Che Puan Sarimah currently lives In KL with her husband YM Tunku Nadzimuddin Tunku Mudzaffar, their 2.5 yr old daughter Tunku Sofia.
She currently emcees events, hosts entertainment TV shows such as Vazz Vaganza on Astro RIA, she hosted the Prestigious Malaysian Film Festival 2022 LIVE on RTM2 and the first ever inaugural LIVE IKON Sports Awards Harian Metro for Mediaprima.

**SI:** From a professional prospective, as an actress, since 1996 to date it will be hosting the AJL Awards (similar to the Grammy’s). I’ve co-hosted three times! Also acting. I start a new Astro TV series playing a Lawyer!

**SI:** Probably Oat… I feel it’s somewhere in the middle. Neutral. Can be a great addition to compliment other colours and is usually creamy and delicious in texture. LOL! Definitely not beige! Hehe.“

**SI:** As a youngster being on holiday with either grandparents and family in Ireland or Malaysia … I grew up learning the depths of both cultures and am very grateful for that.

About mental health awareness campaigns working with government and private sectors. Empati Malaysia, a youth non-governmental organization (NGO) dedicated to fighting for youth’s mental health with empathy, is excited to announce the official launch of its organization and the appointment of Yang Mulia Che Puan Sarimah as its official spokesperson.
Founded by Syahida Zulkarnain, Empati Malaysia aims to promote mental health education, support, and resources to the community through collaborations with organizations such as Pusat Psikologi Jiwa Damai, Pusat Kecemerlangan Kesihatan Mental Kebangsaan, and Jabatan Kebajikan Masyarakat (JKM). The launch event, which will take place on March 25th, 2023, at Liberal Latte, Kuala Lumpur, will be graced by YB Adam Adli Abd Halim, Deputy Minister of Youth and Sports.
The launch event will be a momentous occasion for Empati Malaysia, as it aims to raise awareness and advocate for the mental health of young Malaysians. The organization believes empathy is a powerful tool in promoting mental health and is committed to providing mental health education, support, and resources to the community.
Empati Malaysia has been working tirelessly to promote mental health awareness and support among the youth in Malaysia. With the appointment of Che Puan Sarimah, a well-known personality in the country and an active mental health advocate, the organization hopes to reach a wider audience and make a bigger impact in the community.
Che Puan Sarimah’s passion and dedication to the cause of mental health aligns perfectly with the goals and objectives of Empati Malaysia. As a spokesperson, she will work closely with the organization to raise awareness about mental health issues among the youth and encourage them to seek help when needed.
Attendees can also expect an engaging and informative program during the launch ceremony, with speeches from Empati Malaysia’s founding members and special guests.
